From 620b90d30c08684dc6ebee07c72755d997f9d1f6 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jia-Ju Bai <baijiaju1990@gmail.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Mar 2021 19:44:46 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] mtd: maps: fix error return code of physmap_flash_remove()

When platform_get_drvdata() returns NULL to info, no error return code
of physmap_flash_remove() is assigned.
To fix this bug, err is assigned with -EINVAL in this case

Fixes: 73566edf9b91 ("[MTD] Convert physmap to platform driver")
Reported-by: TOTE Robot <oslab@tsinghua.edu.cn>
Signed-off-by: Jia-Ju Bai <baijiaju1990@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Miquel Raynal <miquel.raynal@bootlin.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-mtd/20210308034446.3052-1-baijiaju1990@gmail.com

diff --git a/drivers/mtd/maps/physmap-core.c b/drivers/mtd/maps/physmap-core.c
index 001ed5deb622..4f63b8430c71 100644
--- a/drivers/mtd/maps/physmap-core.c
+++ b/drivers/mtd/maps/physmap-core.c
@@ -69,8 +69,10 @@ static int physmap_flash_remove(struct platform_device *dev)
 	int i, err = 0;
 
 	info = platform_get_drvdata(dev);
-	if (!info)
+	if (!info) {
+		err = -EINVAL;
 		goto out;
+	}
 
 	if (info->cmtd) {
 		err = mtd_device_unregister(info->cmtd);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/mtd/maps/physmap-core.c`**
- A check was added to the `physmap_flash_remove` function to handle the case when `platform_get_drvdata(dev)` returns `NULL`.
- If `info` is `NULL`, the variable `err` is now assigned the value `-EINVAL` before proceeding to the `out` label.
- This change ensures that an appropriate error code is returned when there is no valid driver data associated with the platform device.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a bug where the function `physmap_flash_remove()` did not return an error code when `platform_get_drvdata()` returned `NULL`. By assigning `-EINVAL` to `err` in this scenario, the patch improves error handling and ensures that the function behaves correctly in cases where the driver data is not available. This change is linked to the previous commit that converted `physmap` to a platform driver, indicating that the issue arose from that transition.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
info = platform_get_drvdata(dev);
if (!info)
```
Reason:
The function `platform_get_drvdata(dev)` can return `NULL` if there is no valid driver data associated with the platform device. When this happens, the subsequent code does not assign an appropriate error return code, which can lead to undefined behavior or incorrect handling during the removal process of the flash device.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
err = -EINVAL;
goto out;
```
Reason:
By assigning `-EINVAL` to `err` when `info` is `NULL`, the code now properly indicates an error condition. This ensures that the function `physmap_flash_remove()` returns a meaningful error code when there is no valid driver data, thus improving error handling and preventing potential undefined behavior.
